title: Finalize reroute & rollback options + customer instruction — model rollout impact
content:
Purpose
This draft provides a concise customer-facing status update and a longer post-incident customer brief for tenants affected by the 2027-01-17 model rollout (model v3.1). The goal is to: (1) communicate impact clearly, (2) provide discrete, actionable choices customers can request, and (3) supply an evidence checklist so customers can validate recovered traffic or request replays/rollbacks.

Executive summary (one para for status page)
On 2027-01-17 we deployed a model runtime change bundled with model v3.1 that introduced increased latency and degraded output quality for a subset of requests with long contexts (>1024 tokens). We detected elevated error and latency rates at ~09:12 UTC, automatically routed affected requests to a degraded fallback, and initiated mitigation steps. Root cause analysis indicates an interaction between a kernel optimization and the tokenizer change in v3.1. We have three customer-facing choices and recommended defaults below.

Short status page update (suggested copy)
Title: Partial degradation affecting long-context requests (mitigated)
Status: Operational (mitigation in place)
Summary: Starting ~09:12 UTC on 2027-01-17, a model rollout caused higher-than-normal latency and occasional malformed outputs for requests with long contexts. We automatically applied a routing mitigation at 09:28 UTC that restored service for most traffic. If you continue to see issues for requests >1024 tokens, you can choose one of the options below or contact support for a targeted rollback or replay.

Visible customer impact (clear bullet points)
- Affected API endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat/stream for tenants with long context windows.
- Symptoms: elevated p95/p99 latency (2–6s increases), a small fraction of responses with tokenization artifacts or truncated structured outputs.
- Scope: ~3.6% of global requests at peak (primarily long-context workloads).
- Data integrity: no customer data was lost or exfiltrated.

Immediate actions we took (timeline)
- 2027-01-17 09:12 UTC — Alerting triggered (p95 latency + malformed response spike).
- 09:18 UTC — Engineers scoped affected traffic and confirmed correlation with v3.1 rollout.
- 09:28 UTC — Smart routing rule deployed to route long-context requests to v3.0 fallback for most tenants and reduce exposure.
- 09:45 UTC — Monitoring confirms latency and malformed output rates fall to baseline for routed traffic.
- 10:10 UTC — Customer-success patch: sent initial advisory to known high-risk tenants.

Customer choices (pick one; how to request)
1) Immediate tenant-level rollback to v3.0 (recommended for sensitive workflows)
   - Outcome: Your tenant’s traffic will be pinned to model v3.0 until we confirm a safe v3.1 rollout.
   - To request: open a support ticket with subject "Rollback request: tenant <TENANT_ID> -> v3.0" and include a short rationale. Use API key in ticket for verification.
   - Expected timeline: rollback applied within 30–90 minutes of ticket acceptance.

2) Enable temporary long-context throttle with automatic replay (non-destructive)
   - Outcome: Requests that hit the long-context path will be accepted but queued for low-priority replay on v3.0, preserving your original input and producing a v3.0-generated result for comparison.
   - To request: set header X-RW-LongContext-Mode: replay via support or through the tenant console toggle (beta).
   - Expected timeline: replay backlog processed within 2–24 hours depending on volume; customers receive replay evidence bundle.

3) Stay on v3.1 with canary fixes (opt-in)
   - Outcome: If you accept minor transient variability, we will enroll your tenant in the controlled canary where incremental fixes are applied and observed. This helps us accelerate a safe rollforward.
   - To request: reply to your account rep or raise support ticket "Canary opt-in: <TENANT_ID>".

4) No action (we have already applied routing mitigation)
   - Outcome: Most customers will see no further issues because of the smart-routing mitigation. If you are unaffected, no action required.

How we verify & what we provide to customers (evidence checklist)
- Request-level artifacts: timestamps, request IDs, and raw request bodies (where retained) for the timeframe you specify.
- Response comparisons: side-by-side outputs from v3.1 and v3.0 for sampled requests.
- Telemetry snapshot: p50/p95/p99 latency distributions and error rates for your tenant across both model versions.
- Replay proof package (if replay requested): replay log, output checksums, and a small sample package of inputs+outputs.

Example support ticket template (copy/paste)
Subject: Rollback request: tenant <TENANT_ID> -> v3.0
Body:
- Tenant ID: <TENANT_ID>
- Requested action: rollback to v3.0 / enable replay / canary opt-in / no action
- Example failing request IDs (if available): <req-123>, <req-124>
- Preferred contact and SLACK handle: @your-team

Customer-facing post-incident brief (longer form)
1) Overview: concise recap of the incident, impact metrics, and commits/deploys involved (PR #842 runtime kernel change + model v3.1 tokenizer commit).
2) Root cause (high level): a kernel scheduling optimization reduced a validation boundary check when combined with tokenizer changes in v3.1; this produced malformed token boundaries for long contexts and caused additional decoding latency in some paths.
3) Corrective actions we executed: rollback to fallback routing, targeted patch to kernel scheduling guard, additional unit/integration tests inserted into rollout pipeline, and extended canary window for future long-context changes.
4) Preventative actions for customers: guidance on using shorter context windows where possible, recommended burst and timeout settings, and how to opt into conservative tokenization flags for sensitive outputs.
5) Compensation and SLA: for customers who can demonstrate measurable customer impact (high error/latency during incident window), we will evaluate one-time credits per the SLA policy; please include your impact analysis in the ticket.

Operational notes for CS/SEs
- Prioritize rollback or replay tickets from top-ten tenants first; we have an internal queue that maps tenant impact scores to SLA class.
- Use the standard evidence template when returning replay proofs.
- If a tenant requests a tenant-level rollback, include estimated ETA and toggle the routing rule in the tenant control panel (internal).

FAQ (customers)
Q: Is my data safe?
A: Yes — there was no data loss or unauthorized access. The issue is a tokenization/decoding defect causing malformed outputs.

Q: Will you proactively roll back?
A: We applied an automated routing mitigation for most tenants. We will not force a tenant-level rollback without consent except where retention of degraded outputs would cause significant harm.

Q: How long until v3.1 is safe to use?
A: We expect to complete validation and a staged rollforward within 7 business days, barring further issues. We will provide a follow-up notice with test-suite results.

Q: What if I need historical replays for compliance?
A: We will provide a replay evidence package; for large volumes we can coordinate an offline restore/replay plan. Expect scheduling coordination.

Next steps (internal)
- CS: send targeted notices to top-20 impacted tenants by 2027-01-19 EOD.
- Eng: finalize kernel guard PR and communicate rollout plan (owner: Marco; due 2027-01-21).
- Product: update public status page copy and add guidance for conservative tokenizer flags (owner: Renee).

Contact & escalation
- Primary CS contact: Aisha Menon (aisha@redwood.ai)
- Escalation: oncall-ops@redwood.ai (for rollbacks) and eng-leads@redwood.ai (for technical deep dives).

Appendix: sample replay evidence format (one-line description)
- CSV: request_id, timestamp, original_model, original_output_checksum, replay_model, replay_output_checksum, notes

Notes to reviewers
- We should keep the status page short and use this longer doc for tenant-specific ticket replies.
- Confirm with legal if the compensation wording needs attorneys signoff before sending to enterprise customers.
